Subject: EU/APAC discovery — synthesis + immediate next steps

Anna — thanks again for a helpful session this morning. Quick synthesis from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of needs
- Primary focus: high consistency for German, French, Spanish (EU) and Korean, Japanese (APAC) across NLU intents + chat fallback.
- Hard constraint: PII redaction and auditability for EU regs (data residency conversation ongoing with ops).
- Target latency: 200ms p95 for short-turn chat flows; batch inference OK for bulk post-processing.

Initial model shortlist (high-level)
- Candidate A: mid-sized family (6–8B FP16 / INT8) — best cost/latency tradeoff for live chat, strong EU morphology handling.
- Candidate B: larger LM (13B quantized) — higher quality on APAC tokenization edge cases but costlier; recommended for pilot on Korean/JP.
- Candidate C: lightweight specialist for reranking/intent detection (2–3B) — use for fast deterministic classification and fallback logic.

Deliverables we’ll share today (attachments + links):
- Locale prompt pack v1 (CSV) — starter prompts and expected outputs across 10 intents per language.
- Benchmarks quickview (PDF) — end-to-end p50/p95 latency and quality slices from our sandbox runs.
- Suggested mutual action plan (XLSX) — timeline and milestones for a 6-week evaluation.

Open questions we flagged in the call
1) Are you able to run a small in-house sample (1000 utterances) for Korean tokenization edge cases, or do you want Redwood to host?
2) For audit logs and retention — what retention window is acceptable for your security team?

Next steps (proposed)
- Jordan: share attachments + HubSpot deal note (this email).
- Neha: recommend exact model variant and quantization profile for the pilot (by EOD).
- Anna: confirm whether LW will share sample utterances or prefers Redwood-hosted run (by Thu 5/20).

Thanks — will sync on a short 30-min pilot kickoff once Anna confirms.

—
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Jordan — the summary is spot on and appreciated. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Tokenization samples: we can provide a 1k sample for Korean and a 1k sample for German by Friday (5/21). Is CSV fine?
2) Retention: our security team prefers 30-day logs with the option for on-demand exports for audits. Anything less than 90 days may be problematic but 30 days is a good starting compromise.
3) Pilot scope: we'd like the pilot to exercise both chat flows and batch intent classification. For budget reasons, we want to start with Candidate A for EU workflows and Candidate B only for JP/KR subsets.

Anna / team — quick note with risk/metric callouts and concrete model recommendations for the pilot. Apologies for the long email; wanted to be explicit.

Risk areas to instrument during pilot
- Tokenization drift (KR/JP): monitor OOV rate and token fragmentation; if token fragmentation increases >8% vs baseline we should surface as a quality regression.
- EU morphology errors (DE/FR): measure slot-filling F1 on the intent set; target baseline >0.88 for adoption.
- Latency regressions during burst: define p95 SLOs per route; pilot should include synthetic burst tests to reach 2x expected QPS.
- False-positives on PII redaction: include a seeded prompt set that contains edge-case PII formats for EU locales.

Concrete pilot model mapping
- EU chat + intent (primary): Candidate A -> recommended variant: "mid-7b-int8-std". Rationale: strong morphology handling in our evals, good cost profile.
- JP/KR chat (edge cases): Candidate B -> "large-13b-q3" for the KR/JP slices only; fallback to mid-7b for cost control.
- Fast intent classifier/reranker: Candidate C -> "lite-3b-clf" (deploy as isolated micro-endpoint).

Artifacts attached to this thread (also on Drive)
- locale_prompt_pack_v1.csv — includes 10 intents × 5 example variants × 7 languages (header docs included).
- benchmarks_quickview_20270518.pdf — sanitized results from sandbox runs, includes per-language BLEU/ChrF and human-audit notes.
- mutual_action_plan_lw.xlsx — proposed milestones: data receipt (5/21), sandbox runs (5/22–5/28), in-prod pilot (6/01–6/14).

Ask from LW
- Please upload the tokenization samples as CSV and share the Drive link; we’ll run them through the KR tokenizer sanity checks as soon as we have them.

I’ll stand up a short monitoring dashboard (latency tokens, OOV, F1 for slot filling) in Redwood Console for the pilot — will share the link by EOD.

—
